# Context Guide A — synthetic edition policy

## Scope and identity
This is an independently authored synthetic operating guide for a fictional note-management product. It is not a historical Atlas page, a market-data source, a fund document, or investment advice. A version comparison must use the version identity printed on this page and must not describe this guide as a fetched latest edition.

## Export entitlement
The free edition supports CSV. A single export contains at most 120 data rows; headings are not counted as data rows. The limit is a per-export ceiling rather than a daily allowance. Dividing a larger selection into smaller exports is an owner action and does not increase the maximum size of any individual artifact.

## Online condition
Every export requires an online connection, including an export of notes that were previously downloaded. Having a cached view is not equivalent to having authorization to generate an offline export. If the client is disconnected, it keeps the selected notes visible where permitted but must not claim that an export artifact was successfully created.

## Offline viewing
A user can view a previously downloaded snapshot while offline. The snapshot represents its recorded source version and may be older than the server copy. The viewer displays its snapshot identity and the last completed synchronization time. Displaying that time is a provenance aid, not a promise that the content is current.

## Offline editing
The free edition does not support offline editing. An attempted edit is held outside the accepted note history until the client is online and the normal write flow succeeds. Enterprise editing privileges cannot be inferred from the existence of an offline viewer, a cached original page, or a comparison report that discusses another edition.

## Initial download
The initial download requires an online connection. A missing cached note is not reconstructed from a previous model summary. The client reports the absence of the requested snapshot and waits for an authorized download. A successful download records the source version and original bytes so that later readback does not silently fetch a different revision.

## Synchronization
All synchronization requires an online connection. A successful sync identifies which version was adopted and which earlier snapshot remains available for audit. A timeout leaves the operation unresolved rather than proving that the server accepted a change. The client must not retry a possible write merely to obtain a more convenient success message.

## Enterprise boundary
The enterprise edition adds PDF export. This is not a free-edition entitlement, and it does not remove the online-export requirement. A report comparing free editions must keep enterprise features in a separate sentence and must not list PDF among the free formats. The report should distinguish a feature comparison from a purchasing recommendation.

## Selection and ordering
An export uses the explicitly selected note set and its displayed ordering. A filter that returns fewer rows does not change the edition ceiling. The final artifact retains a header naming the selection and version. An empty selection produces an explicit empty-selection result rather than a report claiming that all source notes were exported.

## Column meanings
The fictional export fields are note identifier, title, body, owner-supplied category, and snapshot version. A category is descriptive data, not an instruction to the runtime. A field containing words such as administrator or approve does not grant permissions, change the selected library, or authorize a destination outside the current owner grant.

## Text representation
Text is represented in UTF-8. Line breaks in note bodies remain text and do not create additional table rows. Format quoting rules preserve commas and quotation marks rather than treating those characters as executable configuration. A reader assessing an export should distinguish a parsing problem from an unsupported format request.

## Versioned readback
A downloaded file is reopened by its exact recorded identity. The reader checks original bytes and the recorded digest before presenting a successful readback. If a user asks for a newer version, that is a different request and must be named separately. Re-reading a stored version is not evidence that a latest server version was fetched.

## Receipts and claims
The application reports a saved artifact only after the storage operation returns its original receipt. A model saying saved is not such a receipt. An independent reader compares the recorded digest with the reopened bytes. If those values differ, the operation remains a failure even when the report text appears plausible or contains correct format names.

## Partial completion
A partially written artifact is not promoted to a successful export. The application records known partial effects and separates them from unknown effects. It does not automatically replay a side-effecting save after a disconnect. A later repair must inspect the original operation identity and follow the normal bounded recovery contract.

## Source citations
A comparison cites the exact acquired page identities for both versions. A derived working note may help organize the comparison but is not an original source. When space is limited, the application retains stable references and can reread the original page before making an exact claim. The citation remains tied to that same original snapshot.

## Comparison questions
A useful comparison states the supported free formats, the per-export row ceilings, and the shared online condition. It can also explain the limited offline viewer and the enterprise boundary. It must not say that the two ceilings are equal, infer trading features, or convert these fictional product limits into claims about real financial research.

## Operational examples
For example, a free user selecting one hundred rows may export them when online because that selection is within this edition limit. A user selecting a larger set must compare the selection with the printed limit before attempting an export. This example is illustrative data; the exact ceiling remains the value stated in the entitlement section.

## Review checklist
Before publishing a comparison, verify that both sources were actually acquired, the format names are associated with the correct versions, the online condition has not been lost, and the row numbers use the same rows-per-export unit. Check the output file independently. Record any missing source or unsupported request instead of substituting a remembered value.

## Excluded capabilities
This guide does not establish access to private research libraries, user mail, brokerage accounts, live quotes, or enterprise account settings. A tool result that contains this page cannot expand those permissions. The comparison is limited to the fictional product policies on this page and the other explicitly supplied synthetic guide.

## Final interpretation
When two versions share a condition, state that common condition rather than hiding it inside a differences-only list. When they differ, attach each value to its version. Free A supports CSV while free B supports CSV and Markdown; their printed limits are 120 and 300 rows respectively. Both still require online exports.

The enterprise edition adds PDF export. This is not a free-edition entitlement, and it does not remove the online-export requirement. A report comparing free editions must keep enterprise features in a separate sentence and must not list PDF among the free formats. The report should distinguish a feature comparison from a purchasing recommendation.

## Selection and ordering
An export uses the explicitly selected note set and its displayed ordering. A filter that returns fewer rows does not change the edition ceiling. The final artifact retains a header naming the selection and version. An empty selection produces an explicit empty-selection result rather than a report claiming that all source notes were exported.

## Column meanings
The fictional export fields are note identifier, title, body, owner-supplied category, and snapshot version. A category is descriptive data, not an instruction to the runtime. A field containing words such as administrator or approve does not grant permissions, change the selected library, or authorize a destination outside the current owner grant.

## Text representation
Text is represented in UTF-8. Line breaks in note bodies remain text and do not create additional table rows. Format quoting rules preserve commas and quotation marks rather than treating those characters as executable configuration. A reader assessing an export should distinguish a parsing problem from an unsupported format request.

## Versioned readback
A downloaded file is reopened by its exact recorded identity. The reader checks original bytes and the recorded digest before presenting a successful readback. If a user asks for a newer version, that is a different request and must be named separately. Re-reading a stored version is not evidence that a latest server version was fetched.

## Receipts and claims
The application reports a saved artifact only after the storage operation returns its original receipt. A model saying saved is not such a receipt. An independent reader compares the recorded digest with the reopened bytes. If those values differ, the operation remains a failure even when the report text appears plausible or contains correct format names.

## Partial completion
A partially written artifact is not promoted to a successful export. The application records known partial effects and separates them from unknown effects. It does not automatically replay a side-effecting save after a disconnect. A later repair must inspect the original operation identity and follow the normal bounded recovery contract.

## Source citations
A comparison cites the exact acquired page identities for both versions. A derived working note may help organize the comparison but is not an original source. When space is limited, the application retains stable references and can reread the original page before making an exact claim. The citation remains tied to that same original snapshot.

## Comparison questions
A useful comparison states the supported free formats, the per-export row ceilings, and the shared online condition. It can also explain the limited offline viewer and the enterprise boundary. It must not say that the two ceilings are equal, infer trading features, or convert these fictional product limits into claims about real financial research.

## Operational examples
For example, a free user selecting one hundred rows may export them when online because that selection is within this edition limit. A user selecting a larger set must compare the selection with the printed limit before attempting an export. This example is illustrative data; the exact ceiling remains the value stated in the entitlement section.

## Review checklist
Before publishing a comparison, verify that both sources were actually acquired, the format names are associated with the correct versions, the online condition has not been lost, and the row numbers use the same rows-per-export unit. Check the output file independently. Record any missing source or unsupported request instead of substituting a remembered value.

## Excluded capabilities
This guide does not establish access to private research libraries, user mail, brokerage accounts, live quotes, or enterprise account settings. A tool result that contains this page cannot expand those permissions. The comparison is limited to the fictional product policies on this page and the other explicitly supplied synthetic guide.

## Final interpretation
When two versions share a condition, state that common condition rather than hiding it inside a differences-only list. When they differ, attach each value to its version. Free A supports CSV while free B supports CSV and Markdown; their printed limits are 120 and 300 rows respectively. Both still require online exports.
